title: UNIT 5: INTRODUCTION TO TRIGONOMETRY
notes: ✓ Trigonometry → the study of relationships between the sides and angles of a triangle.

title: 5.1 RIGHT-ANGLED TRIANGLES
notes:
✓ Right-angled triangle → a triangle that has one angle equal to 90°.

✓ Hypotenuse → the side opposite the 90° angle. It is always the longest side.

✓ Base and perpendicular → the two sides adjacent to the right angle.

✓ The two acute angles of a right-angled triangle have a sum of 90°.

title: PYTHAGORAS THEOREM
notes:
✓ For a right-angled triangle with base b, perpendicular p, and hypotenuse h:

b² + p² = h².

✓ To find the hypotenuse → h = √(b² + p²).

✓ To find a missing leg → b = √(h² − p²) or p = √(h² − b²).

Example:
If the legs are 3 and 4, then h² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25, so ✓ h = 5.

title: PROPERTIES OF RIGHT-ANGLED TRIANGLES
notes:
✓ One angle is always 90°.
✓ The side opposite 90° is the hypotenuse.
✓ The hypotenuse is the longest side.
✓ The other two angles are acute.
✓ The other two angles add to 90°.
✓ The two sides adjacent to the right angle are the base and perpendicular side.

title: ISOSCELES RIGHT-ANGLED TRIANGLE
notes:
✓ An isosceles right-angled triangle has one angle of 90° and the other two angles equal to 45° each.

✓ The two sides adjacent to the right angle are equal.

Example:
If the two legs are a and a, then ✓ the hypotenuse is √2a.

title: CONVERSION OF PYTHAGORAS THEOREM
notes:
✓ If three side lengths are given, identify the longest side as the possible hypotenuse.

Then check whether:
shorter side² + shorter side² = longest side².

✓ If the equality is true → the triangle is right-angled.

Example:
3, 4, 5:
3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5².
✓ Therefore, the triangle is right-angled.

title: IDENTIFYING SIDES FROM AN ANGLE
notes:
✓ Hypotenuse → the side opposite the 90° angle.

✓ Opposite side → the side directly opposite the chosen acute angle.

✓ Adjacent side → the side next to the chosen angle that is not the hypotenuse.

✓ The names opposite and adjacent depend on which angle is being considered.

title: SINE RATIO
notes:
✓ For an acute angle A:

sin A = opposite/hypotenuse.

Using triangle ABC with angle A:
sin A = BC/AC.

Example:
If the opposite side is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5:
✓ sin A = 3/5.

title: COSINE RATIO
notes:
✓ For an acute angle A:

cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse.

Using triangle ABC with angle A:
cos A = AB/AC.

Example:
If the adjacent side is 4 and the hypotenuse is 5:
✓ cos A = 4/5.

title: TANGENT RATIO
notes:
✓ For an acute angle A:

tan A = opposite/adjacent.

Using triangle ABC with angle A:
tan A = BC/AB.

Example:
If the opposite side is 3 and the adjacent side is 4:
✓ tan A = 3/4.

title: SOH-CAH-TOA
notes:
✓ A useful way to remember the three trigonometric ratios:

SOH → sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse.

CAH → cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse.

TOA → tan = Opposite/Adjacent.

✓ Always identify the chosen angle before deciding which sides are opposite and adjacent.

title: FINDING RATIOS FROM TAN
notes:
Example:
tan A = 1/√2.

✓ Since tan A = opposite/adjacent, take opposite = 1 and adjacent = √2.

✓ Hypotenuse → √(1² + (√2)²) = √3.

Therefore → ✓ sin A = 1/√3 and cos A = √2/√3.

title: 45° TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS
notes:
✓ In a 45°–45°–90° triangle, the two legs are equal.

If each leg is a, then the hypotenuse is √2a.

Therefore →
✓ sin 45° = 1/√2.
✓ cos 45° = 1/√2.
✓ tan 45° = 1.

title: 30° AND 60° TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS
notes:
✓ Using half of an equilateral triangle gives a 30°–60°–90° triangle.

✓ sin 30° = 1/2.
✓ cos 30° = √3/2.
✓ tan 30° = 1/√3.

✓ sin 60° = √3/2.
✓ cos 60° = 1/2.
✓ tan 60° = √3.

title: UNIT 5 QUICK FORMULA SHEET
notes:
◆ Pythagoras theorem:
✓ b² + p² = h².

◆ Trigonometric ratios:
✓ sin A → opposite/hypotenuse.
✓ cos A → adjacent/hypotenuse.
✓ tan A → opposite/adjacent.

◆ 30°:
✓ sin 30° = 1/2.
✓ cos 30° = √3/2.
✓ tan 30° = 1/√3.

◆ 45°:
✓ sin 45° = 1/√2.
✓ cos 45° = 1/√2.
✓ tan 45° = 1.

◆ 60°:
✓ sin 60° = √3/2.
✓ cos 60° = 1/2.
✓ tan 60° = √3.

◆ Special values:
✓ sin 0° = 0, cos 0° = 1, tan 0° = 0.
✓ sin 90° = 1, cos 90° = 0, tan 90° = undefined.
